Hi Elena \u00151

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the kickoff:

1) High-level ask: evaluate a retrieval-augmented conversational assistant for customer support (order status, returns, store locator) across EN/ES/PT.

2) Proposed POC scope (4 weeks):
   - Week 0: kickoff, ingest sample logs & dataset access
   - Week 1: baseline evaluation (existing system vs Redwood models)
   - Week 2: model selection & integration, small tuning/filters
   - Week 3: automated evals + user QA sampling
   - Week 4: handoff, decision & next steps

3) Success criteria (please confirm / edit):
   - Accuracy: >= 85% intent correctness on a 1k sample (weighted across EN/ES/PT)
   - Latency: 95th percentile < 700ms for single-turn queries
   - Cost: avg token cost target to be below $0.015 per query (TBD with traffic profile)
   - Safety/hallucination: < 3% critical hallucination rate on a curated test set

4) Model needs: multilingual support (English + Spanish + Portuguese); fallback for high-load/cost.

Action items:
- Please confirm the success criteria and whether Procurement should be looped in now (cc'd)
- If you can share a small sample (500-2k utterances) that represents typical queries, we can run baselines before kickoff

I'll attach a draft mutual action plan and a brief model perf matrix with candidate open models for the trial.

Perfect - thanks for the sample, Elena. Attached: Redwood-POC-MAP.pdf (mutual action plan) and model-perf-matrix.csv with quick benchmark numbers from our internal runs. High-level model recommendations for the trial:

Primary (balance of cost/quality):
- LLaMA 2 13B (chat, q4_k quantized) - good latency/cost for retrieval-augmented chat; strong cost profile for heavy traffic.

Fallback (low-cost spike handling):
- Mistral 7B Instruct (q4_0) - lower cost, faster token throughput; acceptable for straightforward Q/A and routing escalations to richer models when uncertain.

High-accuracy option (if you opt for quality over cost):
- Falcon-40B-Instruct or LLaMA-2-70B-chat (quantized) - better on nuanced dialogs but higher cost/latency.

Multilingual notes:
- LLaMA-2-13B instruction-tuned variant performs reasonably in ES/PT for common retail queries. If we see gaps, we can apply a small adapter fine-tune on the 1.2k sample + augmented synthetic translations.

Evaluation plan (short):
- Baseline: run sample across current system + the three candidate models.
- Metrics: intent accuracy, slot extraction F1 (order id, store location), 95p latency, hallucination rate (human-labeled), cost per session.

Next steps:
1) Confirm kickoff 2/20 10am PT - I'll send a calendar invite.
2) Procurement: we'll send SLA-draft.docx for review (attached).
3) Tech: Marissa/Aditya will run the baseline on the sample and share results by EOD Wed.

Adding a few technical / ops notes from my side:

- For a 4-week POC with multilingual needs, my recommendation is to start with LLaMA-2-13B (q4_o/q4_k) as primary - it gives the best latency vs quality tradeoff for retrieval-augmented flows.
- Fallback strategy: route to Mistral-7B when request queue depth grows past the threshold OR when model confidence is low (we can use our built-in uncertainty heuristics).
- If the customer wants near-human accuracy on tricky dialogs, allocate a canary route to LLaMA-2-70B-chat (reserved capacity) for those sessions only.

Instrumentation / evaluation checklist:
- Tracing for per-request model selection and token counts
- Token-level cost reporting (console) + per-route latency dashboards
- Small human-eval panel (50-100 samples) across EN/ES/PT to check hallucination & tone

I'll pick up the baseline runs on the sample Elena shared and post results into the Drive link by Wednesday EOD. Also happy to run a quick 20-min tech deep-dive during the kickoff.

Cheers,

Technical confirmation and logistics:

- Model variants & quantization profiles we will use for the POC:
  * llm:llama-2-13b-chat (q4_k) - primary
  * llm:mistral-7b-instruct (q4_0) - fallback/cost-save
  * llm:llama-2-70b-chat (q4_o) - reserved canary for high-difficulty dialogs

- Routing policy: initial traffic to primary; confidence threshold 0.6 triggers fallback; canary route for sessions flagged as "complex" by simple heuristics (long dialog, multi-turn with entities).

- Multilingual approach: prefer native multilingual model behavior + small adapter fine-tune on the 1.2k anonymized Spanish/Portuguese samples. If performance in PT lags, we can add lightweight translation augmentation (EN->PT) for retrieval + answer generation pipeline.

- Instrumentation we will onboard: per-request trace_id, model_used, token_count_in/out, model_confidence, latency_ms. These feed into the Redwood Console dashboards (cost & latency per-route).

POC timeline & ownership (4 weeks):
  - Week0 (2/20): Kickoff - Ben (owner) / Marissa (tech lead) / Elena (customer lead)
  - Week1 (2/21-2/27): Data ingest & baseline runs - Marissa/Aditya (deliver baseline report)
